title: Chemical components analysis of handmade alcoholic beverages with special focus on psychoactive drugs as adulterants
author: Miri, Badakhshan, et al.

steps.title: Prepare calibration standards
steps.instruction: Prepare six‑point calibration curves for ethanol, methanol, acetone and isopropanol at 3, 6, 15, 30, 60, 80 and 100 % v/v using blank distilled water; also prepare HPLC calibration solutions for the targeted psychotropic APIs at appropriate concentrations (e.g., 300–6000 ng/mL) as described in the SOP.

steps.title: Determine LOD and LOQ for volatiles
steps.instruction: Spike distilled water with decreasing concentrations of ethanol, methanol, isopropanol and acetone until a signal‑to‑noise ratio of ≈3 is reached on the GC‑FID; perform six replicate analyses at each level (2–10 mg/L) to establish the LOQ.

steps.title: Determine LOD and LOQ for APIs
steps.instruction: Spike distilled water with low concentrations of each psychotropic API until a signal‑to‑noise ratio of ≈3 is observed on the HPLC‑PDA; perform six replicate injections at each concentration (300–6000 ng/mL) to define the LOQ.

steps.title: Inspect sample appearance
steps.instruction: Record each beverage’s appearance, odor, color and pH (measured with a Metrohm pH meter).

steps.title: Dilute sample for GC analysis
steps.instruction: Pipette 0.4 µL of the alcoholic beverage into a tube and dilute with double‑distilled water to a final volume of 1 mL; mix gently before GC‑FID injection.

steps.title: Perform GC‑FID analysis of volatiles
steps.instruction: Inject the diluted sample into a gas chromatograph equipped with a flame‑ionization detector (GC‑FID) and quantify ethanol, methanol, acetone and isopropanol using the prepared calibration curves.

steps.title: Mix sample with borate buffer (DLLME)
steps.instruction: Add 2 mL of the alcoholic beverage to 5 mL of borate buffer (pH 9) in a tube and stir for 2 min to equilibrate.

steps.title: Extract APIs by DLLME
steps.instruction: Add a pre‑prepared extraction mixture consisting of 300 µL chloroform (extraction solvent) and 2 mL methanol (dispersion solvent) to the buffered sample; vortex until a cloudy emulsion forms.

steps.title: Centrifuge and collect extract
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the tube for 5 min at 3000 rpm; the chloroform phase will sediment at the bottom. Withdraw the bottom extract.

steps.title: Evaporate and reconstitute extract
steps.instruction: Evaporate the collected chloroform extract to dryness under a gentle nitrogen stream; add 25 µL methanol, vortex to dissolve the residue, and transfer to an autosampler vial.

steps.title: Set up HPLC‑PDA system
steps.instruction: Configure the HPLC (KNAUER) with a Eurospher II 100 Å C‑18 column (100 mm × 3 mm, 3 µm); use a mobile phase of phosphate buffer (pH 2.3) : acetonitrile 65:35 v/v at 1 mL/min flow; maintain system pressure at 100–120 MPa; set loop volume to 10 µL; use a PDA‑2800 detector.

steps.title: Inject sample into HPLC
steps.instruction: Inject the 25 µL reconstituted extract into the HPLC system and acquire chromatograms with the PDA detector for quantitative determination of the psychotropic APIs.

steps.title: Perform data analysis
steps.instruction: Process chromatographic data with EZChrom, integrate peaks, and calculate concentrations of volatiles (GC) and APIs (HPLC) using the respective calibration curves; statistical analysis may be performed with SPSS v25 (Chi‑square test).

steps.title: Check dilution integrity if needed
steps.instruction: For samples exceeding the calibrated range, prepare quality‑control spikes in analyte‑free distilled water at concentrations above the LOQ, dilute them into the validated range, and verify that measured concentrations remain proportional (six replicates).

description: The research is a cross-sectional study of 616 samples completely selected from alcoholic beverages referred to the forensic toxicology laboratory of the Forensic Medicine Organization, Markazi province, Iran (March 2022 till March 2023). It should be stated that there is ban and restriction for alcoholic beverages production in Iran. All Samples have been seized from smugglers and distributors in black drug market. Forensic toxicology laboratories are affiliated to the jurisdiction authorities in all provinces in Iran. All the samples have been sent following a complaint or the judge's order for analysing alcoholic beverages in Markazi province, Iran.Quantitative methods had been validated previously for the detection of ethanol, other volatile analytes and also APIs used as a routine analytical method according to the Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) manual in the laboratory. However, some parameters such as LOD, LOQ and linearity were estimated for each analyte of interest. Ethanol, methanol, acetone and isopropanol were analysed in all samples. Analysis was accomplished using gas chromatography with flame ionization detection (GC-FID) for the qualitative and quantitative detection of ethanol, methanol, acetone and isopropanol for forensic toxicology analysis purposes. Routine laboratory practice requires fast and reliable and precise results. Most of the samples that are referred to forensic toxicology laboratories contain unknown amounts of alcohols, so the calibration curve has to be prepared in a wide range of concentrations to cover all concentrations. The six-point calibration curve provides the possibility to determine alcohol concentration in all samples. Calibration curve was prepared at ethanol, methanol, acetone and isopropanol concentrations of 3, 6, 15, 30, 60, 80 and 100 % volume/volume percentage (v/v percent or %v/v) for the linearity assessment.
